native_context: Redis command/key/channel authorization and effective ACLs
taxonomy_note: Planning compatibility lens only. Classify the final observed root cause independently; unsupported mappings stay unassigned.

controls.boundary: Redis command/key/channel authorization and effective ACLs — authoritative consumer
controls.source_trace: Collect Redis version, effective ACL user/selectors, command/key patterns, Pub/Sub rules and actual application command forms. Distinguish key authority from channel authority.
controls.controlled_verification: Using an owned instance/fixture, compare an allowed tenant key and channel with prohibited tenant markers under the same ACL user. Inspect commands that accept multiple keys and the version-specific ACL evaluation path; avoid destructive flush/config operations.
controls.false_positive_discriminator: A broad command category is not alone a cross-tenant read if key patterns constrain the operation. Key patterns do not automatically prove Pub/Sub channel isolation.
controls.remediation_acceptance: Narrow command, key and channel authority using supported version-specific ACLs. Retest legitimate app commands, denied cross-tenant keys/channels and any originally evidenced multi-key path.

coverage_unit: One primary investigative assertion for this technique; not exhaustive coverage. Expand only for genuinely distinct policy/effect assertions in the actual assessment.
